clue.text: Spot bank employee detaining short party representative

parts.note: a TV spot is an advertisement, a commercial

indicators.note: the bank worker holds the shortened party inside, keeping it in

parts.note: a bank teller serves customers at the counter

indicators.note: short means the word for party loses its final letter

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A bank worker holds back a party official in a TV advert scenario.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a stain or a sighting; it is an advertising slot. 'short' drops the last letter of the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a sales agent who visits clients, so a company representative.

clue.text: Catholic inclination to confess, as purification

parts.note: a lean is a tilt or tendency
to sing is slang for informing or owning up to the police

explanation.surface: A Catholic's urge to go to confession, seen as a spiritual washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansing is the act of washing clean, a synonym for purification.

clue.text: Some normal Talisker?

indicators.note: some of the letters of the words that follow are taken, straddling the word break

explanation.surface: An ordinary bottle of a famous Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the letters sit across 'normal Talisker', and Talisker is itself an example of the drink, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Talisker is a single-malt whisky from the Isle of Skye, so an instance of this spirit.

clue.text: Hear piano vaguely with a receiver

indicators.note: vaguely suggests the letters are set out loosely, in a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone listens dimly to a piano through a telephone receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaguely' rearranges HEAR plus P into EARPH; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An earphone is a device that receives sound and delivers it to the ear, so a receiver.

clue.text: Humorist's absolutely huge, not small

indicators.note: not tells us to take the abbreviation for small away from the larger word

parts.note: cosmic means vast, on the scale of the universe
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A comedian with an enormous, never modest, presence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Humorist's' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic is a comedian, someone whose trade is being funny, as a humorist is.

clue.text: Beer and cooking oil surrounding very small depressions

indicators.note: the combined beer and mixed oil go round the abbreviation for very

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of oil are prepared afresh, mixed up

explanation.surface: Beer and frying oil in a kitchen, poured round tiny hollows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges the oil, and 'surrounding' puts the abbreviation for very inside the beer-plus-oil string.
explanation.definitionFit: Alveoli are tiny cavities, such as the air sacs in lungs or tooth sockets, so small hollows.

clue.text: Run after climbing cats, say? You might need this!

definitions.text: Run after climbing cats, say? You might need this!

indicators.note: after puts the run-word behind the other piece
in a down entry, climbing means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: cats are an example of pets
a ladder is a run in a stocking or tights

explanation.surface: Chasing cats up a tree, you will need something to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: STEP from PETS read upwards, then LADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a folding set of steps you might need to reach a cat stuck up high.

clue.text: Stuff for pudding making? One receives deliveries

definitions.meaning: the mixture of flour, eggs and milk from which a Yorkshire pudding is baked
in cricket, the player facing the bowler's deliveries

explanation.surface: Two unrelated phrases: a cook's mixture and someone taking in parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's balls are called deliveries, received by the person at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the liquid mix for puddings and pancakes and the cricketer facing bowling.

clue.text: See 1
Stir the writer to pen ordinary verse

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as in a pen, so the setter's word holds the others

parts.note: the writer is the setter speaking of themself, so me

explanation.surface: A writer is moved to produce some plain poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing, but it means enclose here.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to budge or shift position, a synonym of this verb.

clue.text: Old man securing a metal covering

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the father word grips the rest

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, pa
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: A father fixing a metal sheet to cover something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' wraps the father word round the article and the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin film or sheen that forms over a surface such as bronze, so a coating.

clue.text: American payment inappropriate in tally

parts.note: to tally is to check, as in checking figures
off means unacceptable, as in a remark being a bit off

explanation.surface: An unsuitable charge has crept into an account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a checkoff is union dues deducted straight from wages, so a payment.

clue.text: Stir agitatedly, boarding air journey early in the morning

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the shaken letters go inside the journey

parts.note: a flight is a journey by air

indicators.note: agitatedly means the letters are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous passenger stirs restlessly while getting on a dawn flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitatedly' rearranges stir, and 'boarding' puts those letters inside the air journey just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: First light is dawn, the earliest daylight, so the time early in the morning.

clue.text: A medic gets over it with skill

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A doctor deftly recovers from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link; 'over it' looks like recovery but supplies O and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means deft or skilful, so an adjective describing someone acting with skill.

clue.text: Agonised trendies I ignore, bringing in right advisor on decor

indicators.note: bringing in means the abbreviation for right is added inside the jumbled letters
agonised suggests the words are tortured, twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Tormented fashionable types snub someone, then call in an expert on home styling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agonised' rearranges TRENDIES I IGNORE and 'bringing in' adds R among them.
explanation.definitionFit: An interior designer plans the look of rooms, so gives professional advice on decoration.

clue.text: Ends with clear failing, displaying notoriety

indicators.note: failing suggests the words collapse and fall into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Something ends badly when a clear attempt fails, bringing infamy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two words of fodder; 'displaying' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Esclandre, borrowed from French, means a scandal or public fuss, hence notoriety.

clue.text: City to decline in endless spiral

indicators.note: in places the falling word within the shortened spiral
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a helix is a spiral shape
to sink is to decline or fall

explanation.surface: A city slipping downward in a never-ending spiral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the spiral word's last letter and 'in' puts the decline word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: See 14
Pit with farm animal beyond limits of suburb

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so the animal goes at the end
limits means bounds or encloses, so the end letters of suburb hold the word for with
of points to suburb as the word whose outer letters, its limits, are taken

parts.note: and means with, together with
an ox is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A hollow near a farm on the edge of suburbia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of suburb' does double work: the limits of suburb are S and B, and they limit, or enclose, AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandbox is a sandpit, a shallow pit filled with sand for children to play in.

clue.text: Recalled extra time limiting club's initial form

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in reverse
limiting means enclosing, so the extra word goes round the letter

parts.note: plus means extra or additional

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of club is taken

explanation.surface: A football match recalled for extra time limiting a club's early shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' puts C inside PLUS to make PLUCS; T plus PLUCS, read backwards under 'Recalled', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sculpt is to shape or mould material, a synonym of the verb form.

clue.text: Female upset about distribution of mad source of girlie pics

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed word goes round the jumbled letters
in a down entry upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or woman

indicators.note: distribution means the letters are dealt out and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman angry about the circulation of crazy pictures of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' reads the female word upwards; 'distribution of' rearranges mad, giving DMA, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad mag is a men's magazine known for glamour photos of women, so a supplier of such images.

clue.text: Men suppressing most of home's foul smell

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down or containing, so the soldiers' word encloses the rest

parts.note: the ranks are ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers, so men

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a nest is a home, the 's being a possessive linking it to the rest

explanation.surface: Soldiers stifle a household's horrible odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' as 'the ranks' is the usual crossword sense of soldiers below officer level; 'most of' drops the home word's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankness is the quality of smelling strongly offensive, a stench.

clue.text: Cuddle to hurry up a lot of lovemaking

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word reads upward, in reverse

parts.note: to run is to hurry

indicators.note: a lot of means most, so the final letter goes

parts.note: sex is lovemaking

explanation.surface: A cuddle leads quickly on to a great deal of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RUN into NUR, and 'a lot of' cuts SEX to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse can mean to hold closely and tenderly in the arms, as one cuddles a baby.

clue.text: Indian politician in middle of rights issue at the outset

parts.note: the two middle letters of rights are G and H, written out literally as a phrase

indicators.note: at the outset means the first letter of issue is taken

explanation.surface: A leader of India embroiled in a dispute over rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'rights' is 'G and H', spelt in full; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement, and Indira and Rajiv Gandhi were prime ministers.

clue.text: Secure article in trap

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the trap word

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for game
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Fix an item firmly in a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin trap is an old hunting snare.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to obtain it, the verb's sense of acquiring or winning.

clue.text: Transport on mountain heading for top tavern

indicators.note: heading means the head, the first letter, of top

parts.note: a bar is a tavern or pub

explanation.surface: A ski-lift rider heads for the summit inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like travelling towards; it picks T.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a ski lift that tows skiers up a slope, so mountain transport.

clue.text: It's the last thing you'll be denied here

definitions.text: It's the last thing you'll be denied here

parts.words: It's the last thing you'll be denied here
parts.note: the last thing in life is dying; in this event you come close to it yet are refused it and survive

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about being refused a final item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last thing' is death itself, which you approach but are denied.
explanation.definitionFit: Such an episode is when someone almost dies and recovers, often reporting a tunnel of light.

clue.text: See 26
